title: 15 — What's New in the Lakehouse, 2026
html:
15 — What's New in the Lakehouse, 2026

The one idea: in 2026 the lakehouse converged. Iceberg v3 shipped across vendors, Delta moved to catalog-managed tables, catalogs became the interoperability layer, governance moved to tags and policies, and document AI and agents moved into SQL and the catalog. This is a dated list of what changed, so you know which notes and habits are already out of date.

1. How to read this list

  • Dates are as reported by the sources found on 2026-10-26. Where sources disagree, both are given.
  • "Secondary" means a blog or news source, not the vendor's own docs or release notes. Check those items before relying on them.
  • Each item links to the chapter that explains it.

2. Open formats and catalogs

When What Chapter
Dec 2025 Spark 4.1 released (secondary date): Spark Declarative Pipelines open-sourced, Real-Time Mode for stateless streaming 06
Dec 2025 ODCS v3.1.0: relationships, stricter validation, executable SLAs. v3.0 contracts stay valid 13
Feb 2026 Apache Polaris becomes a top-level Apache project (19 Feb) 03
Feb 2026 Parquet project announces native variant support (secondary) 04
Early 2026 Delta Lake 4.1: catalog-managed tables, with the catalog as coordinator and source of truth 03
Apr 2026 Delta Lake 4.2: synchronous UniForm (Iceberg metadata at commit time). HMS support for UniForm deprecated 03
Apr 2026 DuckLake v1.0, production-ready, with DuckDB 1.5.2 11
Apr 2026 Databricks lists Iceberg v3 as Public Preview (Runtime 18.0 and above) 02
May 2026 Snowflake reports Iceberg v3 GA. Iceberg Java 1.11.0 (20 May) adds v3 deletion vectors, row lineage, shredded variant writes, and a REST scan-planning client (secondary) 02
Jun 2026 Delta Lake 4.3 routes catalog-managed operations through Unity Catalog's Delta REST APIs 03
Jul 2026 ADBC 24: Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery and DataFusion drivers move to the ADBC Driver Foundry 04
Jul 2026 Polars Cloud 0.6.3 adds a distributed Iceberg sink (another index lists May). Polars' streaming engine gains an Iceberg sink 11
2026 Iceberg v4 proposals: adaptive metadata tree, single-file commits, relative paths. Not a released spec 02

3. Databricks platform

When What Chapter
Dec 2025 Vector Search reranker GA (8 Dec) 09
Jan 2026 Iceberg format support announced in the Delta Sharing protocol (headline only) 08
Feb to Mar 2026 Lakebase GA on AWS (February) and Azure (3 March) 10
Mar 2026 Databricks Asset Bundles renamed Declarative Automation Bundles (16 Mar). Commands unchanged 06
Mar 2026 Agent Bricks becomes the umbrella for Databricks AI. Document classification and extraction UIs in Public Preview. Health indicators for tables (Public Preview) and anomaly-detection alerts (Beta) 09, 13
Apr 2026 ai_parse_document GA (16 Apr). Governed tags GA (2 Apr). Metric views reported GA (secondary, some pages still say preview) 09, 05, 07
May 2026 ABAC policies, governed tags and automated data classification announced GA 05
Jun 2026 Vector Search relaunched as Databricks AI Search (forum-reported date 1 June): BM25, hybrid, reranking 09
Jun 2026 OIDC-secured sharing for Iceberg REST clients. Cross-region sharing across regulatory domains (Public Preview). Lakebase Postgres 18 support 08, 10
Jul 2026 Unit testing for pipelines, including AUTO CDC, in Beta 06
Aug 2026 Lakebase Postgres APIs GA (14 Aug) 10
Sep 2026 Sharing foreign Iceberg and foreign Delta tables with OpenSharing GA. Lakebase Search GA (secondary) 08
2026 ai_extract and ai_classify listed GA in the latest release notes (older pages say preview) 09
2026 Managed MCP servers still Public Preview per the docs (updated September 2026) 09
2026 Free Edition: up to 3 apps, serverless only, one 2X-Small warehouse 07

4. What this means in practice

  1. Default to managed tables in Unity Catalog (Delta or Iceberg): you get predictive optimization, governance and open access through REST.
  2. Plan v3 adoption per engine. You can't downgrade, so check every reader first.
  3. Move access control to governed tags and ABAC instead of per-table masks.
  4. Document AI can start in SQL (ai_parse_document, ai_extract, ai_classify), with self-hosted models where data must stay in-region.
  5. Retrieval is hybrid by default (BM25 plus vectors plus reranking), with citations.
  6. Bundles are "Declarative Automation Bundles" in new docs. Same CLI.
  7. Laptop-scale engines are first-class Iceberg citizens: DuckDB, Polars and Daft all read and write through catalogs.

5. Common mistakes

  1. Trusting a blog post's GA claim. Check the vendor's release notes, and note the date you checked.
  2. Copying 2024 code samples. Names changed (DLT to Lakeflow pipelines, dlt to pyspark.pipelines, Vector Search to AI Search, Asset Bundles to Declarative Automation Bundles).
  3. Assuming one cloud's status applies to another. Lakebase, for example, differed by cloud.

6. Exercise (30 minutes)

Pick three items from section 3 that matter to your work, open their current release-note pages, and record today's status and date. Note any item whose status changed since this list was written.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. What were Databricks Asset Bundles renamed to, and when?
  2. Which Iceberg version added v3 deletion vectors and row lineage in Java?
  3. What is the state of Iceberg v4?
  4. When did ai_parse_document become GA?
  5. Which ADBC drivers left the Apache Arrow project?

Answers

  1. Declarative Automation Bundles, on 16 March 2026.
  2. Iceberg Java 1.11.0, released 20 May 2026 per the board report.
  3. Proposals with design documents and prototypes, not a released spec.
  4. On 16 April 2026, per the release notes.
  5. Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery and DataFusion, which moved to the ADBC Driver Foundry.

8. Sources

  • Apache Iceberg releases: https://iceberg.apache.org/releases/
  • Delta Lake blog: https://delta.io/blog/

  • ADBC 24: https://arrow.apache.org/blog/2026/07/28/adbc-24-release/
